PullRequest.Title: Update Component Explorer packages
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

- update `@vscode/component-explorer` and the Vite plugin to `0.2.1-140`
- update the CLI to `0.2.1-143`
- update the webpack plugin to `0.3.1-132`
- preserve all unrelated transitive dependency versions

Follow-up to #334375, which merged on September 4.

## Validation

- `npm ci --ignore-scripts --dry-run`
- `npm --prefix build/rspack ci --ignore-scripts --dry-run`
- `npm --prefix build/vite ci --ignore-scripts --dry-run`
- `npm exec -- component-explorer --help`
- verified all four installed package versions with `npm ls`
- pre-commit hygiene hook

The Vite build initializes Component Explorer 0.3.0 and discovers all 85 fixtures, then reaches pre-existing fresh-checkout failures from uncompiled built-in extensions and JSONC inputs.

Scenarios.Scenario: Cold or warm npm installation for the root, Vite, and Rspack workspaces
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Package-manager resolution, registry fetch on a cold cache, integrity verification, archive extraction, and lockfile installation must complete before builds or Component Explorer tooling can run.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch the updated Component Explorer, CLI, Vite-plugin, and webpack-plugin tarballs from the npm registry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One tarball fetch per distinct updated package on a cold package cache; warm caches can reuse the integrity-addressed archives. The explorer tarball is shared by name/version but each independently installed workspace may perform its own package-manager cache lookup and filesystem materialization.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same number and shape of registry fetches occurred for the prior package versions; only tarball versions, URLs, and integrity hashes changed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold misses block installation; warm cache hits avoid registry transfer but installation still materializes packages.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Verify and extract package archives and write dependency trees for three npm workspaces.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Four distinct updated packages across three workspace installs, with the explorer package represented in each workspace; transitive dependency sets shown in the lockfiles remain unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The prior versions required equivalent package extraction and had the same declared transitive dependencies.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number and compressed/uncompressed size of updated package tarballs across the three independently installed workspaces.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Controlled by npm's installer and cache; the repository changes do not add a loop, limiter, queue, or concurrent installation path.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Registry artifacts may be reused from npm's content-addressed cache by integrity. Version and integrity changes force an initial cold fetch, as every dependency upgrade does; subsequent installs can be warm. No application cache or negative cache is changed.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that only package identities change at this boundary and that lockfile dependency graphs are unchanged; no evidence establishes extra network or filesystem work beyond the normal one-time cold fetch for new versions.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The repository does not expose old/new tarball byte sizes, but there is no changed dependency cardinality or mechanism supporting a regression claim.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the diff changes package artifacts but does not show increased boundary cardinality, repeated installation work, or retained state.

Scenarios.Scenario: Starting or building the Vite Component Explorer and discovering fixture modules
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Vite loads its configuration and plugins, the Component Explorer plugin scans the configured src/**/*.fixture.ts include, and build mode bundles all discovered fixtures before a production build completes; dev startup similarly requires plugin initialization and discovery before serving.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Glob and read fixture modules under src for Component Explorer discovery and bundling.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One configured repository-wide discovery pass over files matching src/**/*.fixture.ts, followed by bundler module reads for the effective set of matched fixtures and imports.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same plugin configuration, include glob, and build:'all' behavior existed with version 0.2.1-137.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Plugin initialization/discovery is on Vite startup and production-build critical paths.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Transform and bundle the discovered fixture graph in Vite/Rolldown.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Scales with the deduplicated module graph reachable from all matched fixtures, not one independent full build per fixture.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The prior Vite plugin occupied the same plugin slot with the same options and dependency graph.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks production build completion and contributes to development-server readiness.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The effective count of matching fixture files and their deduplicated imported module graph.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Vite/Rolldown owns module scheduling; no concurrency setting, batching policy, or per-fixture process fan-out changes in this diff.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm Vite development sessions may reuse bundler/module caches; cold process startup scans and transforms the configured graph. No cache key or invalidation code is changed in the repository diff.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in path reachability and pre-existing repository-wide discovery; low confidence in any performance delta because no changed implementation is available and lockfile dependencies are unchanged.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Implementation changes inside the external package tarball are not present in the supplied diff, so their internal CPU or I/O behavior cannot be established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No high-confidence finding: upgrading an opaque plugin version does not itself prove added scanning, repeated transforms, cache defeat, or startup latency.

Scenarios.Scenario: Starting the Rspack Component Explorer development server or static build
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Rspack evaluates configuration, finds a free local port, initializes the Component Explorer plugin, discovers src/**/*.fixture.ts, compiles the workbench and fixture graph, and then serves or emits assets.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Discover fixture files and compile/read their transitive TypeScript, CSS, font, and theme assets.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One include glob over src/**/*.fixture.ts and one deduplicated bundler graph for the matched fixtures; static builds additionally copy two pre-existing icon-theme directories.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same ComponentExplorerPlugin include and Rspack configuration ran with webpack-plugin 0.3.1-130 and explorer 0.2.1-137.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Discovery and initial compilation block server readiness or static-build completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Bind and serve the generated application over localhost.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One development server, with request count driven by browser use; no additional server or remote request is added.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical local server configuration and port selection existed before the package bumps.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Local server readiness is required by CLI serve/render workflows, while individual requests are on interactive render paths.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of matching fixtures, size of their deduplicated dependency graph, and browser request frequency during a session.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Rspack owns graph compilation and dev-server request scheduling; lazyCompilation remains false and no new worker, queue, or parallel invocation is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A warm long-running dev server can reuse its compilation state; cold startup compiles the graph. The diff changes no filesystem watch, module-cache, or invalidation configuration.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that startup and bundling are performance-sensitive but unchanged at repository level; insufficient evidence of a changed mechanism.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: External package internals are unavailable in the reviewed patch, so no delta in plugin algorithm or emitted bundle can be proven.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: versions change, while scan scope, compilation mode, server behavior, and dependency graph remain stable.

Scenarios.Scenario: CLI-driven Component Explorer serve, render, Playwright tests, and CSS-order analysis
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The CLI starts or attaches to a local Rspack server, waits for readiness, launches browser-backed renders, writes screenshots/manifests, and callers read output files. Each Renderer.render invocation is awaited before that caller can inspect results.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Launch component-explorer serve from Playwright or launch a fresh Node CLI render process from the CSS-order tools.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One serve process per Playwright web-server session; one render subprocess per explicit Renderer.render call, with multiplicity controlled by pre-existing scan/bisect callers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same commands and subprocess cardinality used CLI version 0.2.1-140.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Serve readiness blocks test startup; each render subprocess blocks its corresponding analysis step.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Communicate with the local Component Explorer HTTP server and browser during serve/render.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One configured localhost server and browser requests/renders driven by selected fixtures; max worktree slots remains 1.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same local HTTP server configuration, attach flow, and maxSlots:1 constraint existed before the CLI upgrade.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Local server and browser responses are on the render critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Write screenshots and manifests, then read manifest.json and image outputs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One unique target directory and manifest per render invocation; screenshot count scales with effective matched fixture entries, with hash paths deduplicating identical images by default.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same per-render output directories, hash-path default, and manifest reads existed with the previous CLI.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: CLI output writes and manifest reads must complete before each analysis invocation returns.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize render input to JSON and parse the resulting manifest.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One input serialization and one manifest parse per render invocation; manifest size scales with the selected fixture entries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical caller-side serialization and parsing occurred before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs synchronously around each awaited CLI subprocess but is unchanged by the version bump.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of CLI render invocations, effective fixtures selected by each regex, output image cardinality after hash deduplication, and manifest size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Playwright starts one configured web server; component-explorer worktree maxSlots is 1. Renderer calls launch fresh processes, but actual parallelism depends on unchanged callers; the diff adds no Promise.all, queue, or burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A running server can serve repeated renders without repeating server startup; each Renderer.render intentionally uses a fresh target and subprocess. Hash-based output paths deduplicate identical images within render output. No cache or coalescing behavior is changed by repository code.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the existing subprocess/I/O path and its scaling; insufficient evidence that the upgraded package changes its cost.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The CLI tarball's internal delta is not visible, so there is no evidence that version 0.2.1-143 changes browser launches, output bytes, retries, or fixture cardinality.
Scenarios.Verdict: No high-confidence performance issue can be attributed to the diff. Reporting would require evidence from the changed package implementation or measurements tied to a concrete mechanism.

Scenarios.Scenario: Interactive rendering of Component Explorer fixtures in the browser
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The explorer runtime and fixture definitions are bundled by the selected plugin, loaded by the local browser, and React renders the selected fixture; this work is on the first-display and subsequent fixture-selection paths.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Load locally served Component Explorer JavaScript, styles, and fixture assets.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Initial asset requests scale with emitted chunks and selected fixture dependencies; subsequent navigation may reuse the browser HTTP/module cache.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same explorer runtime package role and local bundler/server paths existed at the prior version.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Initial local asset loading blocks first render; cached resources reduce repeat latency.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: React renders the Component Explorer UI and selected fixture components.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One active selected fixture and its variants/render tree at a time, with updates driven by user/test interactions; repository code provides no evidence that this cardinality changed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Fixture definitions already imported and used the explorer runtime; only the external runtime version changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous rendering contributes directly to interactive display latency.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Emitted bundle size, selected fixture render-tree size, variant count, and interaction frequency.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Browser rendering is scheduled by React/browser event loops; the diff exposes no changed scheduling, listener fan-out, worker, or render batching behavior.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Browser asset caching can make later loads warm; fixture rendering state is session-local. No repository-visible cache key, lifecycle, or retention change is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that this scenario consumes the upgraded explorer package, but no confidence in a regression mechanism from version metadata alone.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The package implementation and emitted bundle delta are absent, so increased CPU, DOM work, bytes, or retained objects cannot be demonstrated.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: dependency metadata alone cannot establish eager UI construction, repeated rendering, larger serialization, or memory retention.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all six changed files and every diff hunk. The PR only updates four Component Explorer package versions and lockfile artifact metadata while preserving declared transitive dependencies and repository configuration. Traced installation, Vite/Rspack startup and fixture discovery, CLI subprocess/render flows, filesystem/serialization work, localhost serving, and browser rendering. No concrete diff-introduced performance mechanism is present, and no regression fix can be proven from repository code.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
